project: defender — an LLM SOC-analyst agent (python, pytest, uv)

gate.test: cd defender && uv run pytest tests/ -m "not live and not gate" -n auto --dist loadfile --ignore tests/e2e/test_540_box_boundary.py
checks: the baseline-ratcheted custom lints under scripts/lint/lint_*.py (monkeypatch, unsafe-jsonl-io, raw-git-subprocess, unanchored-default, vulture, duplicate-helpers, …) — each blocks only on a NEW finding, and each documents an inline-suppression escape hatch in its own module
gate.notes: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is the source of truth — run what it runs; don't trust this list to stay current. Running in a git worktree? The shared `.venv` editable install points at the main checkout — prepend `PYTHONPATH=<worktree-root>` to the pytest call or you test the wrong tree.

tests.harness: defender/tests/e2e/_replay_harness.py — a new scenario is a few lines of `Turn(...)`, not fresh plumbing. Build on it rather than inventing parallel machinery.
tests.idioms: Fakes enter through the entry point's injection seams (a `deps` parameter, a constructor argument), never `monkeypatch.setattr` — CI ratchets new setattr sites (`scripts/lint/lint_monkeypatch.py`).

learning_queue.note: ADDED BY #921's GROUNDING: `evals/harness.py::materialize` is a writer of this sink's shape that no import-following census sees — it `shutil.copy`s a scenario's own findings.jsonl into `<tmp>/defender/learning/_pending/findings.jsonl` and copytrees a `runs/` fixture beside it, then runs the real author against that tree. It is a HARNESS edge, not a loop edge, and it is the reason a row-shape change has a second consumer. Also worth pinning for the next census: the findings channel has ONE gate (`CorpusAuthorConfig.gate`, wired to `learning/author/lessons/run.py::_gate_findings`), called once per tick over EVERY keyed row of findings.jsonl — so two directions in one file share one gate and one batch, and the gate indexes entry['finding_id'|'run_id'|'direction'] directly inside drain's stuck-recording guard, where a missing key takes the whole tick's batch to `<channel>.stuck.jsonl`. UPDATED BY #922: `QUEUEABLE_FINDING_TYPES` is now the ONLY finding-`type` vocabulary left, and `learning/judge/enqueue.py::_validate_row` is its one production consumer. The set it used to be shadowed by — the pipeline judge's document validator in `core/validate.py` — was deleted with that judge.

learning_run_dir.note: RE-GROUND BEFORE USE (#922). Every writer and reader this census listed was the old learning pipeline's — the per-case cycle that minted the dir, the actor that wrote its story, the judge that wrote its comparison, the direction table and judge visualizer that read them — and all of them are deleted. The PATH is still live: `learning_run_dir` is a field on every `StageContext`, and the surviving stages (the findings curator, the forward-check, the lead author, the family judge) each write under one. But the shape of what lands there changed with the pipeline, so the honest census is empty rather than a stale list, and the next spec that touches this sink has to take it fresh. The two grep terms that named the retired functions' own artifacts left with them.

run_dir.note: Four writers were added after #771's phase-F reconciliation found the same hole in three instruments at once. The driver's fault-exit trace write (`write_text("")` onto the fixed tool_trace.jsonl name observe.write_trace also owns) is one of the two sites that issue reported and was missing from the test census, the write lint's gate list AND this list. The queries-table append is the query tool's SECOND artifact — the payload write was censused, the table was not. The lead-claim hook and the atomic helper are the two the original grep could not see. EVERY ENTRY MUST NAME A SYMBOL THAT RESOLVES: three of the four added here did not (a leading underscore the driver's entry point does not have, an actor id where the code symbol was `_revert_strays`, and a render-lane function renamed at some point), and a resolver following a name that resolves to nothing gets the same answer as one following a row that was never written. This list seeds the next run's census, so a gap here becomes a gap in every downstream instrument. `scrub` stays under readers deliberately: #771's scan verdict is written OUTSIDE the tree it judges (§7 D8), so the walk remains a pure reader of the run dir and the marker belongs to no run-dir writer census.

drain_worktree.note: #869's grounding added the two writers the SPAWNED-AGENT-ONLY reading of this root missed. `synthesize_drafts` is a HOST-side writer into the worktree's catalog — it mkdir+writes `<catalog>/{system}/_draft/{suffix}.md` from a model-supplied `query_id` BEFORE the agent is spawned, which is the whole of #869's C12 reachability finding and was invisible to a census that only listed the agent's file tools. `commit_corpus` is the sink's actual commit (git add over the `defender/skills` pathspec) and the last gate any path rule sits in front of. The readers added are the ones that ask the tree a MEMBERSHIP question: the git-status scope walk that applies the per-actor path rule, the `_draft/` discovery that turns a directory name into a handoff `system`, and the two per-actor path rules themselves. THE THIRD READER THIS ORIGINALLY LISTED WAS `pitfalls_curator.py::_is_real_system`, THE `SKILL.md` PROBE — and #869 DELETES that symbol, so the entry that seeds the next run's census would have named a symbol resolving to nothing, which this block's own rule forbids and which a resolver cannot distinguish from a row nobody wrote. Replaced with the threaded membership readers that survive the change (`_pitfalls_path_rule`, `_skills_path_rule`); the resolver they are threaded from, `learning/leads/declared_systems.py::declared_systems`, is deliberately NOT listed yet because it does not exist until write-code-from-spec builds it — add it in the same commit that does, or this list under-counts the membership readers by one.

episode_dir.note: Declared by #947's grounding. AT b8a63e66 `capture.py:130-136` composes it as `resolve_runs_base()/'episodes'/<id>/` — a sibling of the run dirs, inside the runs base. #947 MOVES BOTH ENDS OF THAT, and this note is written against the design, not the base: (1) the episodes root becomes a CONFIGURED location (`DEFENDER_EPISODES_BASE`), outside both the runs base and the checkout, with NO default derivation — a reader that re-derives it from the runs base silently restores the containment hole the relocation closed (#947 §7 round 2, F5-EPISODE-ROOT); and (2) the three sibling run dirs move UNDER it, at `{episode_dir}/runs/`, so the episode dir is a PARENT of run dirs rather than their sibling. `cli.py::episode_dir_for` is the symbol whose semantics change: it is the production resolver every reader of an episode must go through once the root is configured, and the one to follow instead of re-composing a path. The old safety clause here read 'a SIBLING of the run dirs, never inside one, so it is not bound into any box' — that is verbatim the reason `capture.py:134`'s waiver states, and #947 REFUTES it on that reason (claim C26): the episode dir now contains three rw box binds. The conclusion survives on a different ground, recorded as an examined no: the bind is the run dir alone, `served/` and `worlds/` stay unreachable from inside a box, and every archive read goes through the `_run_paths.artifact_file` / `stage_tables` screens. Rewrite `capture.py:134`'s waiver text in the same commit that moves the root. Today it holds only `served/`: `prime_base` writes `served/base.jsonl` once and `Ledger.record` appends `served/<world_id>.jsonl`, one writer per file — which is the whole of the launcher's parallel-safety premise. The directory is created as a side effect of `_io.append_jsonl`'s parent mkdir, NOT through `guarded_mkdir`, and NOTHING anywhere removes an episode dir: both `prepare_episode` and `prime_base` treat an existing one as a permanent refusal. #947 adds family.yaml, staged.yaml, review.yaml, provenance.json, worlds/<X>/ AND runs/<sibling>/ here — add those writers (staging.py, review.py, archive.py, _family.py) IN THE COMMIT THAT CREATES THEM, not before: a row naming a symbol that resolves to nothing is indistinguishable to a resolver from a row nobody wrote. ADDED IN THE COMMIT THAT CREATED THEM, as the sentence above requires: `write_family` (family.yaml), `record_staged` and `_record_teardown_failure` (staged.yaml and the teardown block of review.yaml), `review` (review.yaml), `archive_episode` (worlds/<X>/), and `cli._record_episode_outcome` / `_write_family_stamp` (the episode's own outcome and its provenance.json). The readers gain the two derived readers, the staging record's own reader and the manifest loader. ADDED BY #921's GROUNDING (re-verified at base 9f4e8247, where #947's relocation HAS landed: `episodes_root()` is $DEFENDER_EPISODES_BASE with no default derivation, refused inside the runs base and inside REPO_ROOT, and the sibling run dirs live at {episode_dir}/runs/ via cli.RUNS_SUBDIR). The writer this list was missing is `observe.RequestLogger`: `learning/branch/seams.py::model_seam` builds StageContext(learning_run_dir=episode_dir), and `_pydantic_stage.run_stage` writes every questioner and comparator call's FULL wire stream to `<episode_dir>/wire_logs/<agent_id>_trace.jsonl` through `observe.stage_trace_path` (guarded_mkdir) + `open_guarded` — the seam's own docstring says 'THE TRACE LANDS IN THE EPISODE'. #921's per-world judge calls multiply that stream by worlds x draws and each one carries the whole 10-32K-token prompt verbatim, so a census that lists only judge.yaml and worlds/<X>/judge/ under-counts the writers by the largest artifact in the tree. `_archived_labels` is added beside `verdicts`/`delta_o` because it is the reader that turns `worlds/` into the label set both of them iterate. STILL TRUE and worth keeping: NOTHING removes an episode dir, and `capture.py:134`'s lint-unguarded-tree-write waiver STILL reads 'the episode archive is `runs_base/episodes/<id>/`, a sibling of the run dirs' — refuted text that the commit moving the root was supposed to rewrite and did not.

elastic_corpus.note: Declared by #947's grounding as an EMPTY-WRITER root, which is the fact worth recording: at b8a63e66 nothing in defender/ creates an Elasticsearch index or alias (re-verified: the only `_aliases`/`put_alias` hits are a yaml dumper flag and the model-provider alias table). Every listed reader reaches the cluster through the one read-confined door, `elastic_adapter._http_json` -> `confinement.guard_outbound` -> `confine_read_endpoint(verb_class='r')`, whose elastic allowlist is exactly `/*/_search POST`, `/_query POST`, `/_cluster/health GET`, `/api/status GET`. #947's corpus staging is the FIRST writer; it must call `transport.docker_exec_curl` directly, and note that `guard_outbound` is also the capture recorder, so a write door that skips it records nothing anywhere but `staged.yaml`. #947 LANDS THAT FIRST WRITER and this row now names it: `staging._Door` reaches `docker_exec_curl` directly with PUT/POST/DELETE, outside `guard_outbound`, so `staged.yaml` is the only record any of these writes happened. The host-side reads are listed beside them because `_count` and `_resolve/index` are deliberately absent from the adapter's read allowlist — they exist only on this door.

conventions.dangerLens: adversarial input — alert data is attacker-influenced by definition, and malicious input is well-formed on purpose. Use this as write-tests' fourth enumeration lens unless the change's danger zone is clearly elsewhere (environment/resource, or concurrency when the design admits parallel invocation).

codeGraph.notes: defender is a namespace package (no defender/__init__.py; pyproject at defender/, not the repo root), so pyrefly's import root defaults to defender/ and `defender.x` imports silently resolve to Unknown. searchPath is relative to configDir: `..` = repo root (makes `defender` a top-level package, mirroring pytest's pythonpath=['..']), `.` = defender/. The pyrefly-refs helper writes a temp configDir/pyrefly.toml from these and removes it per run.
